newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia malt barley demand steady - Grainco.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia malt barley demand steady - Grainco.

text.p: Overseas demand for Australian malting barley is holding steady for the first half of 1997, the Queensland state grain cooperative Grainco Ltd said on Monday
"The international market, particularly the Chinese buyers, will look to cover their remaining first-half 1997 requirements in early 1997," Grainco said in its weekly report.
"Potential European and Canadian production will then become available on the world market to compete with Australian malting barley around July/September 1997," it said.
Analysts estimate Australia will produce about six million tonnes of barley in the current harvest.
Domestically, prices were steady over the Christmas period, with Grainco's malting barley cash bid for the week ending January 3 at A$188 a tonne, delivered Brisbane.
A subdued domestic sorghum market in recent weeks was attributed by Grainco to the Christmas season slow down compounded by further rain in southern and central regions of Queensland.
"Internationally, values continue to be under pressure from a steady to lower corn futures market and expectations of aggressive selling from both U.S. and Argentine sources," Grainco said.
Indications that Argentina's sorghum crop continues to build could hurt Queensland growers, who will be competing against Argentine sorghum for Japanese business.
Domestically, values in southern Queensland continue to trade at a premium to exports, Grainco said.
However, the premium is slowing eroding as the market becomes more comfortable with production following the recent rains, it said.
"In central Queensland, many growers, particularly in the northern highlands, are still waiting for further rain before beginning planting," Grainco said.
In cottonseed, new crop export prices currently equate to between A$100 and A$110 a tonne, ex-gin basis, Grainco said.
"Little business, if any, is being done at these levels, with the export market taking the view that the crop is large and as such prices will ease further," it said.
Domestic oilseed values moved lower in the last week, with new crop black sunflowers settling at A$315 a tonne, delivered Brisbane and A$310 a tonne delivered Moree for January-April, it said.
